claim_tested: A yeast FSH-family serine hydrolase acts on a glycerophospholipid
key_finding: Purified recombinant Fsh1p (the FSH3 paralog) is a lysophospholipase specific for lysophosphatidylserine; FSH3 was not assayed
context: S. cerevisiae, purified recombinant protein plus overexpression lipidomics
confidence: moderate for FSH1, none for FSH3
limitations: Paralog, not the target gene. The GO term derived from it (GO:0004622) names phosphatidylcholine while the assay used phosphatidylserine

claim_tested: FSH3 carries an existing lipase or phospholipase annotation
key_finding: FSH3 has GO:0016787 hydrolase activity (IBA, GO_REF:0000033) only, with GO:0003674 and GO:0008150 both ND (GO_REF:0000015); CC GO:0005634, GO:0005737 (IBA) and GO:0005777 peroxisome (IDA, PMID:36164978)
limitations: Absence of annotation is not absence of activity

claim_tested: FSH3 has a cellular role that constrains its molecular function
key_finding: H2O2 raises FSH3 mRNA and protein; fsh3-delta grows better under H2O2; FSH3 overexpression causes ROS accumulation and cell death that requires NUC1
limitations: Overexpression phenotype; no molecular activity measured; no lipid species quantified

claim_tested: FSH-family overexpression phenotypes reflect lipid catabolism
key_finding: FSH1 overexpression triggers apoptotic markers including phosphatidylserine externalisation
limitations: Phenotype is downstream; PS externalisation is an apoptosis readout, not an enzymatic result

claim_tested: The human relative of FSH3 is a phospholipase
key_finding: OVCA2 (Q8WZ82) is annotated GO:0106435 carboxylesterase activity by IDA; FSH1 carries GO:0016788 by IDA from the same work
context: human recombinant protein, ester substrate library
limitations: Retrieved via GO/UniProt; preference is for alkyl esters, a chain-length preference rather than a headgroup preference

claim_tested: Yeast glycerophospholipid deacylation requires an additional hydrolase
key_finding: PLB1, PLB2, PLB3 and NTE1 account for most or all observed glycerophosphodiester production in S. cerevisiae
context: S. cerevisiae, review of characterised activities
limitations: Review; does not exclude a minor additional contributor

claim_tested: Pocket size at the nucleophile predicts substrate class
key_finding: Across six crystal structures with known physiological substrates, cavity volume vs substrate heavy-atom count gives Spearman rho=-0.06 p=0.91 and tunnel length rho=+0.03 p=0.96; LPLA2, a certain diacyl-PC hydrolase, has the smallest cavity (342 A^3) and TLL lipase has none detectable
limitations: Static conformations; lids closed in TLL and LPLA2; the metric is uninformative, so FSH3 measurements cannot be interpreted

claim_tested: Interfacial apolar surface at the active-site mouth predicts lipid substrate
key_finding: Near-site apolar patch: APT1 1475, APT2 1281, TLL 1043, BioH 673, OVCA2 586, FSH3 551, MGL 498, FSH1 389, LPLA2 266, SFGH 0 A^2. FSH3 sits in the soluble esterase range but LPLA2 ranks second lowest
confidence: high for the measurement, low for its discriminating power
limitations: Conformationally gated feature; does not separate the reference classes

claim_tested: Conserved basic and aromatic residues form a phosphocholine headgroup site
key_finding: Triad and elbow invariant (G12, F116, S117, D180, H209 = 1.00; Q15 0.92, Q118 0.98, F153 0.95). Candidate cationic anchors unconserved: K59 0.06, R61 0.04, K154 0.08. Only R187 (0.89) and R82 (0.75) are conserved basics and OVCA2 has Glu187 and Ser82. Pocket vs background class conservation 0.66 vs 0.55, p=0.028; identity 0.44 vs 0.35, p=0.19
context: 65 single-domain fungal PF03959 proteins, 28-53 percent identity
limitations: Conservation of a site is evidence about selection, not about catalysis; the cap region is also the lowest-confidence part of the model (pLDDT<70 at 69-73 and 83-89)

claim_tested: The AlphaFold model supports pocket measurement
key_finding: Core 3-230 median pLDDT 95.4; residues 231-266 below 50; cap loops 69-73 and 83-89 below 70, and these loops form the ceiling of the pocket
limitations: Low-confidence cap means the pocket ceiling, and therefore its enclosed volume, is the least reliable part of the model
